correctness.rationale: Let \(B=I-R^{\mathsf T}R\). Exact multiplication gives \(B_{11}=vz^3[4-(v+1)z]/4\) and \(\det B=vz^4(vz-2)[z((vz-1)^2+3)-8]/16\). The cubic is strictly increasing. Its roots and the first-minor sign cover all \(v,z>0\), including the nonstrict endpoint. A one-to-one root parametrization yields the unique global maximum \(H(3/8)=8/3\). Exact eigenvalues and singular values at that point confirm spectral radius \(1/3\) and operator norm \(1\). The packaged checker passes symbolic identities and two-sided numerical boundary samples; the proof is algebraic, not experimental.

value.rationale: The canonical minimal hypocoercive system dissipates energy in only one coordinate. Its exact all-vector timestep criterion, nonmonotone dependence on coupling, and unique optimal normalized step \(8/3\) provide an actionable sharp stability map. At that optimum the spectral radius is \(1/3\) while the operator norm is \(1\), a precise energy-versus-eigenvalue mismatch. This motivates the exact invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
